Drop an altitude from to and notice that the triangle is congruent to triangle , so this triangle also has a ratio of with respect to triangle . We can let and be x and let be . We can split into 2 -- triangles with hypotenuse . The base of these triangles is , and since each of these triangles is similar to the triangle we just crafted (let this triangle be ), we have a neat way to find the value of . We can say that the base of one of the new -- triangles we crafted is , and since the hypotenuse is , we don't need to work with any radicals at all! We can multiply the hypotenuse by the base in each of the smaller triangles of , add the values together, put the result as the numerator of the fraction with the hypotenuse times the base of , and set this expression equal to .

When we actually work this out, we get that the numerator will be and the denominator will be , and we set this equal to .

We then solve the equation for x.

\begin{align*} \frac{2x^2}{(840-x)^2} &= \frac{8}{9} \\[10pt] \frac{x^2}{(840-x)^2} &= \frac{4}{9} \\[10pt] \sqrt{\frac{x^2}{(840-x)^2}} &= \sqrt{\frac{4}{9}} \\[10pt] \left| \frac{x}{840-x} \right| &= \frac{2}{3} \\[10pt] \frac{x}{840-x} &= \pm \frac{2}{3} \end{align*}

\begin{array}{rcclr} \frac{x}{840-x} &= \frac{2}{3} &\quad \lor \quad& \frac{x}{840-x} &= -\frac{2}{3} \\[10pt] 3x &= 2(840-x) &\quad \lor \quad& 3x &= -2(840-x) \\[10pt] 3x &= 1680 - 2x &\quad \lor \quad& 3x &= -1680 + 2x \\[10pt] 5x &= 1680 &\quad \lor \quad& x &= -1680 \\[10pt] x &= 336 &\quad \lor \quad& x &= -1680 \end{array}
